title: Whales of the Poles
objective: After this level you can describe the whales that feed in polar seas.
summary: Humpbacks commute: summer feasts in polar seas, winter calving in the tropics, up to about 8,000 km away. Only belugas, narwhals and bowheads stay in the Arctic all year.

cards.headline: Some whales swim about 8,000 km just to reach their summer meal.
cards.body: Others never leave the ice at all. The polar seas have two kinds of whale: the commuters and the locals.

cards.headline: The commuters
cards.body: Humpback whales spend the summer in cold, food-rich polar waters, straining Level 75's krill and small fish through their baleen. In winter they head for tropical breeding grounds to mate and have their calves, and some populations swim about 8,000 km between the two. The fat they build up in summer carries them through the winter. They eat in the cold and raise their young in the warm.

cards.headline: Summer visitors, year-round locals
cards.body: The Arctic gets summer visitors too: humpbacks, minkes and fin whales arrive from the south and leave again as it cools. But only three whales live in the Arctic all year: the beluga, the narwhal and the bowhead. The narwhal's famous tusk is actually an enlarged left tooth. One very long tooth.

cards.fact: A bowhead whale can break through sea ice about 20 cm thick with its head.
cards.context: Its large, reinforced skull makes a handy icebreaker when it needs a breath. Under its skin sits the thickest blubber of any whale, about 43 to 48 cm. And it's built to last: studies suggest bowheads may live more than 200 years. Blubber, a hard head and a very long life: made for the ice.

questions.prompt: The three whales that live in the Arctic all year round are the _____ whales.

options.label: humpback, minke and fin
options.rationale: Those are summer visitors that leave as it cools.

options.label: blue, humpback and beluga
options.rationale: Blue whales and humpbacks don't stay all year.

options.label: narwhal, orca and sperm
options.rationale: Only the narwhal is one of the three residents.

questions.explanation: Only the beluga, the narwhal and the bowhead live in the Arctic year-round.

questions.prompt: Match each whale with what it's known for.

pairs.right: The thickest blubber of any whale

questions.explanation: Some humpback populations swim about 8,000 km between feeding and breeding grounds. The narwhal's tusk is an enlarged left tooth. The bowhead has the thickest blubber of any whale.

questions.prompt: Like Level 45's leatherbacks, humpbacks feed in one place and breed in another. Where do humpbacks have their calves?

options.label: In cold polar waters, near their food
options.rationale: That's where they feed, in summer.

options.label: On the beaches where they were born
options.rationale: That's the turtles' way; humpbacks head to tropical breeding grounds.

options.label: Under the Arctic sea ice
options.rationale: Only belugas, narwhals and bowheads stay there all year.

questions.explanation: Humpbacks feed in polar waters in summer, then head to tropical breeding grounds to mate and have their calves.
